parsed.body: The request cannot be fulfilled because a comparison‑based sorting algorithm cannot achieve O(n) worst‑case time complexity. The Ω(n log n) lower bound for comparison sorts proves that any algorithm that solely relies on element comparisons must take at least n log n time on some inputs. Consequently, it is impossible to simultaneously satisfy all of the following constraints: O(n) worst‑case time, stability, in‑place operation with O(1) extra space, and being purely comparison‑based. The only way to achieve linear worst‑case time is to use non‑comparison sorts (e.g., counting sort or radix sort), which violate the comparison‑based requirement. Therefore, the task is theoretically infeasible under the given constraints.
